rulings.model: The helper returns zero when there is no Schedule C; IRS line 15 is the Schedule SE line 13 deduction for any self-employment, such as farm or partnership income, and no refusal covers that case.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 93, Line 15: "If you were self-employed and owe self-employment tax, fill in Schedule SE to figure the amount of your deduction." Self-employment income other than Schedule C (farm income on Schedule F, partnership income on a Schedule K-1, church employee income, and since BUG-0233 income as a minister, a member of a religious order who has not taken a vow of poverty, or a Christian Science practitioner) is named in scope.schedule1 ("Any income or adjustment requiring Schedule 1 other than the ones this tool asks about separately ..."), which refuses Form 1040 line 8 and line 10 and every line after them, so within scope only a Schedule C reaches Schedule SE, and person.se_line13 is that deduction. Unchanged by the fix round apart from the clergy wording, which widens the screen.

rulings.model: The IRA worksheet uses $89,000 for married filing separately who lived apart all year; the helper uses $10,000 for MFS regardless of the line 20 checkbox.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 97, IRA Deduction Worksheet line 2: "Single, head of household, or married filing separately and you lived apart from your spouse for all of 2025, enter $89,000 ... Married filing separately and you lived with your spouse at any time in 2025, enter $10,000"; p. 96: "Married persons filing separately. If you weren't covered by a retirement plan but your spouse was, you are considered covered by a plan unless you lived apart from your spouse for all of 2025." The model says the helper uses $10,000 for married filing separately regardless of the line 20 checkbox. Both rules are for married filing separately only, and a married filing separately return is refused at the return level (s3.mfs on scope.ready: "The rules for a married filing separately return ... are outside this tool. Married filing jointly is supported.", i1040gi p. 14). On a joint return the worksheet's own spouse rule ($246,000 for the person not covered) is applied (person.ira_not_covered_joint). Line 20 copies the worksheet total; unchanged by the fix round. Project stands.

rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 91, Line 8f: "Enter the total of the amounts from Form 8889, lines 16 and 20." Line 20 (Part III, income from failing to remain an eligible individual during a testing period) arises from a qualified HSA funding distribution or from a testing period that began in an earlier year (a last-month-rule testing period that begins in December 2025 cannot be failed in 2025); both are refused by f8889.unsupported ("a qualified HSA funding distribution from an IRA in 2025 ... failing to remain an eligible individual during a testing period that began in an earlier year"), as the line's citation says. Within scope line 20 is zero and person.hsa_taxable is line 16. Project stands.

rulings.model: IRS Pub. 525 says 'These rules don’t apply to scholarship or fellowship awards. See Scholarships and fellowships, later'; the restatement puts a 'scholarship prize' on line 8i.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: model error; p525 p. 36, Scholarships and fellowships, Prizes: "Scholarship prizes won in a contest aren't scholarships or fellowships if you don't have to use the prizes for educational purposes. You must include these amounts in your income on Schedule 1 (Form 1040), line 8i, whether or not you use the amounts for educational purposes." The p. 35 sentence the model quotes ("These rules don't apply to scholarship or fellowship awards") concerns scholarships and fellowships proper; a contest prize that need not be used for education is a line 8i prize, as the question says. Project stands.

rulings.model: IRS line 8j is activity-not-for-profit income; line 8l covers rental of personal property only 'if you engaged in the rental for profit but were not in the business of renting such property.' The restatement excludes rental of personal property altogether.
rulings.ruling: Ruling: scope; i1040gi p. 91, Line 8j, "Activity not engaged in for profit income. See Pub. 525", and Line 8l, "Income from the rental of personal property if you engaged in the rental for profit but were not in the business of renting such property". The question excludes the rental of personal property from line 8j, and scope.schedule1 ("Any income or adjustment requiring Schedule 1 other than the ones this tool asks about separately ..."), which refuses Form 1040 line 8 and line 10 and every line after them names "rental of personal property" without a for-profit qualifier, so a rental of personal property not for profit (which would belong on line 8j) and one for profit (line 8l) are both refused rather than computed. A refusal by a cited scope screen; no computed amount is wrong. Unchanged by the fix round.
